title: Evolution keeps turning other crustaceans into crab look-alikes
body: Carcinisation is the repeated evolution of a crab-like body: a flattened, widened shell with the tail tucked underneath. It has happened independently several times, mostly among anomurans, the group that includes hermit crabs. King crabs, for example, evolved from hermit crab ancestors and still have lopsided abdomens, a leftover from ancestors that lived in coiled snail shells. A compact body that shields vital organs may explain why evolution keeps landing on this design.
